pharm: Mucolytic that depolymerizes mucopolysaccharide fibres in bronchial secretions, reducing sputum viscosity and promoting expectoration; a synthetic derivative of the alkaloid vasicine.

May be taken with or after food; take with plenty of fluid
Avoid especially in the first trimester unless clearly necessary (limited data)
Excreted in breast milk in animals; not recommended during breastfeeding
Use with caution in severe renal impairment
Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment
Cough/sputum response; skin and mucosal reactions
summary: Bromhexine is a mucolytic (secretolytic) agent used to thin viscid bronchial secretions and ease expectoration in respiratory disorders with excessive or tenacious mucus. It is a synthetic derivative of vasicine and the parent of the active metabolite ambroxol. It is generally well tolerated; mild gastrointestinal upset is the most common effect, and rare severe cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) have been reported. Adequate fluid intake supports its mucolytic effect. Bromhexine is NOT approved by the US FDA; this record is based on European SmPC/BNF and international product information.
indications: Secretolytic (mucolytic) therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary disorders associated with abnormal mucus secretion and impaired mucus transport (productive cough)

dosage.c: Productive cough / mucolysis (adults and children >12 years)
dosage.d: 8-16 mg three times daily (commonly 8 mg three times daily)
dosage.n: Take with adequate fluids; per EMA/BNF product information

dosage.d: 4 mg two to three times daily
dosage.n: Per product information; check local formulary
Per product information; not for very young children unless directed

moa: Bromhexine increases the proportion of serous bronchial secretion and reduces mucus viscosity by depolymerizing acid mucopolysaccharide fibres in the sputum, thereby liquefying tenacious secretions and facilitating their expectoration and mucociliary clearance. It also stimulates production of surfactant. Bromhexine is metabolized to ambroxol, which contributes to its activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bromhexine or any excipient
relative: History of gastric or duodenal ulcer (mucolytics may disrupt the gastric mucosal barrier)
Conditions where large volumes of liquefied secretions cannot be cleared (impaired cough)
monitor: Skin and mucous membranes (rare severe cutaneous reactions)

preg: There are limited human data. Avoid use, particularly during the first trimester, unless considered clearly necessary by the prescriber.
lact: Bromhexine passes into breast milk in animal studies; its use is not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in severe renal impairment (metabolites may accumulate); follow product information.
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment, as bromhexine is hepatically metabolized.

moderate: Antitussives (e.g., codeine) - concurrent use may cause stasis of liquefied secretions because the cough reflex is suppressed; avoid combining
Antibiotics (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, erythromycin, doxycycline) - bromhexine may increase their concentration in bronchopulmonary secretions (generally regarded as beneficial)
interactions.food: May be taken with food; ensure good fluid intake.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; avoid excess.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference described.

serious: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis - rare)

monitoring: Skin and mucosal reactions (discontinue at first sign)
Tolerance in patients with peptic ulcer history
counsel: Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medicine - it helps loosen and clear mucus
Stop the medicine and seek medical help if you develop a skin rash, blisters, or sores in the mouth
Do not combine with cough-suppressant medicines unless your doctor advises
Take with or after food if it upsets your stomach
See your doctor if your cough lasts more than a few days or worsens
pk: Mucolytic effect develops over the first days of treatment
Plasma peak about 1 hour after an oral dose
Approximately 6.5 hours (terminal longer due to tissue redistribution)
Store below 25-30 C; protect from light and moisture per product information
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record reflects EMA SmPC / BNF and international product information
Bromhexine is the prodrug-like parent of ambroxol, its principal active metabolite
Rare but serious skin reactions (SJS/TEN) have been reported - stop the drug if skin or mucosal lesions appear
Avoid combining with antitussives, which can cause pooling of liquefied secretions
Adequate hydration is important to support mucolysis
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for your next dose, skip the missed dose - do not take a double dose.
overdose: No specific symptoms of overdose are established; high doses may cause gastrointestinal upset. Management is symptomatic and supportive; routine gastric decontamination is generally unnecessary unless a very large amount has been taken.
